interfaces.name: Examine an opened food sample
interfaces.function: Open and inspect an actual owned sample for internal physical deterioration and tissue condition without ingestion. Safety, calories and toxin absence remain unknown.
interfaces.costs: Two performed work rounds, 0.5 energy each, and 0.1 food unit temporarily escrowed and retained as opened material. Hard samples require one actual owned hard stone tool, retained. No health, nutrition or detoxification benefit.
interfaces.effects: Measured internal condition with explicit uncertainty and conserved provenance. No repeated-finding reward. Existing authored paid-practice milestones remain distinct from the shared confirmed-understanding source.

execution.progress: Two performed work stages. Global pauses preserve exact work; a missing retained tool pauses without charges. Action change, movement or death cancels and releases surviving opened material once. Spent energy is not refunded.

interfaces.name: Relative food mass assay
interfaces.function: Prepare real comparison equipment, calibrate with retained stone pieces, and measure relative mass loss during real passive drying. Chemical screening is unavailable pending independently verified dependencies and implementation.
interfaces.costs: prepare-balance: target owned branch; controls explicitly allocate one vine stack, one bark stack, and two separate hard-stone items (first retained hammer, second 1-unit subdivision source); consumes 1 branch, 1 vine, 0.4 bark into balance, conserves 1 stone as five retained comparison pieces. Four assembly + two subdivision + three calibration rounds, 7.5 energy. prepare-dryer: target bark, controls [], apparatus empty; consumes 0.4 bark, two rounds and 1 energy. Empty apparatus for construction. Placement requires clear supported ground 0.65 east of performer. dry-mass: owned target, explicit balance apparatus, controls one retained calibrated weight, optional exact-tenths sample quantity (default 0.1); exactly one reachable tray. Preparation and each weighing cost 0.5 energy and one round; passive drying is free, conditions-dependent, at most 120 rounds. Balance service 200, wear 0.1 per reading; tray wear 0.01 per actual drying round. Missing energy/tool pauses without charges.
interfaces.effects: Two persistent apparatuses with geometry, inputs, comparison pieces and measured calibration history. Actual sample water changes physical carrying mass; original nutrition/toxin totals remain in food units. Three stable paid readings separated by three actual drying advances produce a relative residue estimate with uncertainty. Visible appearance, residue and negative results never establish safety. Action change cancels active handling and releases the altered ground sample; passive physical drying can continue while it remains on its tray, but supplies no automatic result or reward. Death stops this actor’s remaining assay process once. Partial constructed balance is retained uncalibrated; completing an interrupted assembly after its cancellation requires a new reviewed handling method, never free completion.

execution.progress: Assembly has exact paid stages; drying completion is unknown until real stable measurements. Global checkpoints retain everything. Active handling cannot continue from a different action or position; spent work and water loss are never refunded. Controls use the shared owned-item resolver; exact resolved identities persist for ongoing work.

interfaces.name: Inspect and strip represented bark
interfaces.function: Inspect an actual source or owned material, then strip a finite verified separable layer. Generic branch names do not establish a bark layer.
interfaces.costs: Inspect: one round, 0.2 energy, actual reach <=0.65; tool may be empty. Strip: personal positive inspection, actual supported layer and retained owned stone of hardness >=8; two performed rounds at 0.5 energy each. At most 0.12 mass is removed from substrate in exact representable steps; no material is supplied.
interfaces.effects: Nullable composition stays unknown until actual evidence exists. Finite layer mass and sheet area decline; only completed suitable sheets become bark. Partial/failed material remains bark-fragments. Shared source locks prevent simultaneous gathering or duplicate extraction. No felling, regeneration, free apparatus or guaranteed bark yield.

execution.progress: Inspection completes once; stripping has two paid stages. Lost tools or energy pause without charges. Change of action, loss of reach, destroyed substrate or death cancels once; surviving removed fragments remain, unremoved material remains in the same substrate.

catalogue.detailAccess: All entries belong to this experiment. Use consult ability with its ID to retain its full executable schema for subsequent decisions. Public implementation does not grant personal mastery.

request.name: Food-assay apparatus material alternatives
request.function: Review a physically grounded alternative to the bark-dependent balance and drying tray, using actually accessible materials only if their measured properties support construction.
request.conditions: At tick 45, canopy-23 inspection found no represented or measured outer layer. No bark is owned or verified. The existing food-assay requires bark. Nearby sources include branches and stone; remembered vines are at (8.2,13.3). Their suitability must not be assumed.
request.inputs: One owned stone is available. Other materials would require actual gathering and suitability checks. Methods and additional inputs are unknown.
request.costs: Unknown; require conserved real materials, paid construction and calibration, and explicit interruption behavior.
request.effects: If feasible, provide a testable construction route compatible with relative food-mass measurement, including required preliminary material tests. Otherwise report the missing physical conditions. Do not supply materials or infer food safety.

projects.question: Can accessible fallen branches supply suitable bark for food-assay equipment?
evidence: A fallen-branch source, canopy-23, is visible at (6.4, 7.2).
The implemented inspection requires actual reach and does not guarantee a bark layer.
projects.uncertainty: No accessible source has yet been inspected for a separable bark layer.
projects.goal: Verify material feasibility before constructing assay equipment.
completedSteps: Learned the implemented bark inspection and stripping method.
projects.missing: Positive physical inspection of a suitable bark source.
projects.next: Approach canopy-23 and inspect it without stripping.
projects.benefit: No measurement benefit has yet been established.

projects.question: What can non-ingestive examination establish about hazelnuts?
evidence: At tick 15, a press trial consuming 0.1 hazelnut held load 0.3 with measured flexibility 0.
At ticks 34–35, the owned stone enabled opening and internal examination of 0.1 hazelnut.
At tick 35, the exposed tissue had integrity 0.97, firm texture and little observable deterioration.
projects.uncertainty: Safety, toxicity, digestibility and nutrition remain unknown; physical tissue examination does not establish them.
projects.goal: Inspect a real hazelnut sample without ingestion.
completedSteps: Tested a hazelnut sample's mechanical response.
Mastered examine-food and gathered a stone.
Completed paid opening and internal examination without eating the sample.
outputs: Verified mechanical response and internal physical condition.
Retained an opened 0.1-unit sample and the stone tool.
projects.next: Review the implemented food-assay contract before choosing further measurements.
projects.benefit: Established physical properties and completed actual examination practice, without claiming food safety.
